title: Blue Sky Ideas in Artificial Intelligence Education from the EAAI 2017 New and Future AI Educator Program
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (EAAI 2017 symposium/track context noted in paper)
extended_summary:
This paper is not the requested 2025 secondary-school writing study. Instead, it is a collection of short position pieces produced for the EAAI 2017 New and Future AI Educator Program. The central question is how AI education should evolve in three broad areas: incorporating ethics into AI curricula, teaching AI at secondary-school and early undergraduate levels, and making AI education more interdisciplinary for non-engineering domains.

Rather than reporting an empirical intervention, the paper assembles conceptual proposals from multiple contributors. These include peer-learning models that pair AI students with students from other disciplines, Montessori-inspired student-centric discovery learning, early K-12 exposure to AI concepts through games and puzzles, embedding ethics across AI topics, using real-world high-stakes problems to teach AI/ML, making AI algorithms accessible through hands-on non-coding activities, rethinking the institutional context for AI ethics, a proposed 12-week secondary-school AI course using the General Video Game AI framework, and structured ethics training prompts for AI students.

The populations discussed are broad and prospective rather than studied empirically: secondary school students, K-12 learners, undergraduate and master’s students, PhD candidates/postdocs, and educators. The context spans classroom, lab, and blended-learning ideas, but these are proposed implementations rather than observed deployments. No sample, school site, or measured outcomes are reported.

The main conclusion is that AI education should be made more accessible, interdisciplinary, ethically grounded, and engaging for younger learners and early-career educators. The paper argues for active, project-based, peer-supported, and socially responsible approaches to AI instruction, but it does not test these claims with empirical data.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual 'blue sky ideas' paper from the EAAI 2017 New and Future AI Educator Program, not an empirical study. It does not report a methodology, sample, intervention evaluation, or measured outcomes relevant to secondary-school writing.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational intervention is implemented or tested, and no impact estimates or outcome data are reported. Therefore there is no evidence of impact on student writing or any other measured domain.
